regions.name: International billfish and IGFA slams
regions.intro: A billfish slam counts different kinds of billfish. The IGFA awards belong to individual anglers; crews also talk about boat slams.

terms.meaning: One angler catches any three eligible billfish species in one calendar day under IGFA rules.
One angler catches any four eligible billfish species in one calendar day under IGFA rules.
One angler catches any five eligible billfish species in one calendar day under IGFA rules.
One angler catches all nine listed billfish categories over a lifetime under IGFA rules. Any spearfish species fills the spearfish place.
A crew completes a slam with catches from several anglers aboard one boat. IGFA requires one angler for its awards.

regions.name: US Gulf Coast and Louisiana
regions.intro: A speck means a seatrout along the coast. Head into Louisiana’s freshwater, and names such as sac-à-lait and gaspergou take over.

terms.meaning: The local name for spotted seatrout, a saltwater drum.
The Louisiana name for crappie, including both black and white crappie.
The Louisiana name for freshwater drum.
The Louisiana name for bowfin, also called grinnel.
Gulf Coast names for cobia.
A Louisiana name for white bass.
On the Alabama coast, this name covers sand seatrout and silver seatrout.
An Alabama coastal name for tripletail.
A redfish, speckled trout, and flounder caught in the same day, as used by Mississippi Gulf Coast anglers.

regions.name: Texas Gulf Coast
regions.intro: The usual Texas slam has a red, a trout, and a flounder. Down near South Padre, snook changes the game.

terms.meaning: The traditional one-day combination of redfish, spotted seatrout, and southern flounder.
A redfish, spotted seatrout, and snook caught in one day; this local version replaces the flounder with snook.
The South Texas slam plus a tarpon in the same day.
A big adult redfish. Anglers use bull for large females as well as males.
Short for spotted seatrout, also called speckled trout.
A large spotted seatrout, usually an older female.
A fish within the length range that the local harvest slot allows. The range depends on the species and rules.

regions.name: Carolina and Georgia Lowcountry
regions.intro: A spottail is a redfish here. On a high tide, its tail can show you where it feeds in the grass.

terms.meaning: A redfish, speckled trout, and flounder caught during the same day.
A local name for red drum, also called redfish.
A redfish feeds head-down in shallow water with its tail above the surface.
terms.example: There’s a red tailing beside that grass.

terms.meaning: Redfish that move onto normally dry marsh flats during unusually high tides to feed, often on fiddler crabs.
A large adult redfish; Lowcountry anglers also target these fish around offshore reefs and ledges.

regions.name: Florida mainland
regions.intro: Florida has several named slams, each with its own fish list. The FWC award program gives one angler 24 hours.

terms.meaning: The FWC award requires red drum and spotted seatrout, plus either flounder or snook, within 24 hours.
The FWC award requires dolphinfish, sailfish, and wahoo within 24 hours.
The FWC award requires cobia, great barracuda, and king mackerel within 24 hours.
The FWC award requires sheepshead, Florida pompano, and a whiting within 24 hours.
The FWC award requires bluefish, Spanish mackerel, and ladyfish within 24 hours.
A big, heavy fish, especially a bass. It is praise for the catch, with no single size threshold.

regions.name: Florida Keys
regions.intro: The Keys grand slam means bonefish, permit, and tarpon. A snook turns that day into a super grand slam.

terms.meaning: A bonefish, permit, and tarpon caught in the same day.
A bonefish, permit, tarpon, and snook caught in the same day.
The familiar nickname for tarpon, from its silver scales and impressive size.

regions.name: Chesapeake Bay and Mid-Atlantic
regions.intro: Rockfish means striped bass on the Chesapeake. A citation is an award for a qualifying catch, rather than just a big-fish compliment.

terms.meaning: The local name for striped bass.
A Virginia Saltwater Fishing Tournament award for a fish that meets the species’ weight or release requirements.
A juvenile drum; the name can mean a young red drum or black drum.
Short for weakfish, also called gray seatrout.
A large dolphinfish.
A large bluefish.

regions.name: New England and Montauk
regions.intro: A schoolie and a cow are both striped bass, but very different catches. A blitz can put either one within a cast.

terms.meaning: A small striped bass, often part of a school.
A large striped bass.
A burst of surface action as predators attack baitfish, often with birds above them.
terms.example: There’s a blitz just beyond the rocks.

terms.meaning: Young Atlantic menhaden, a small baitfish that can draw striped bass into a surface frenzy.
Two everyday names for tautog.
The local name for summer flounder.
A local name for winter flounder.
A very large summer flounder. On The Water uses 10 pounds or more for its doormat target.

regions.name: Great Lakes
regions.intro: Great Lakes crews talk about kings, lakers, and steelhead. Lake Michigan’s grand slam brings five salmon and trout species into one outing.

terms.meaning: The Lake Michigan version requires Chinook, coho, lake trout, brown trout, and steelhead in one outing on the same day.
A Chinook salmon.
A lake trout.
The Great Lakes name for a lake-run rainbow trout that enters tributaries.
Short for brown trout.
A summer-run strain of steelhead that supports the midsummer Lake Michigan tributary fishery.

regions.name: Upper Midwest and ice country
regions.intro: On the ice, a slab means a good crappie. A hammer handle is the small pike that gets there first.

terms.meaning: A large crappie.
Ice-covered water; a hardwater trip means a trip to fish through the ice.
A small, slender northern pike, including a young fish or one with slow growth.
A large yellow perch.

regions.name: Pacific Northwest and coastal British Columbia
regions.intro: The salmon names often tell you when a fish returns or how big it is. In British Columbia, a tyee starts at 30 pounds.

terms.meaning: An immature Chinook salmon; this is a familiar name in Puget Sound fisheries.
A spring-run Chinook salmon.
A male Chinook salmon that returns to spawn a year earlier than most adults.
A Chinook salmon of at least 30 pounds. Tyee Club recognition also requires the club’s tackle, location, and catch rules.

regions.name: Alaska
regions.intro: Kings, reds, silvers, dogs, and humpies are Alaska’s five Pacific salmon targets. Lodge anglers call the complete set a salmon grand slam.

terms.meaning: All five Alaska Pacific salmon species on one trip. The Alagnak lodge usage allows a week.
A Chinook salmon.
A sockeye salmon.
A coho salmon.
A chum salmon.
A pink salmon.
Another local name for chum salmon.
The IGFA lifetime award requires one angler to catch Atlantic, Chinook, sockeye, chum, pink, and coho salmon under IGFA rules.

regions.name: California and Southern California boats
regions.intro: Southern California deck talk gives familiar fish some lively names. A goat, a ghost, and a checkerboard are three different catches.

terms.meaning: Local names for California yellowtail.
Nicknames for white seabass.
A California sheephead.
A kelp bass.
A Pacific barracuda.
The local boat name for bocaccio, which is a rockfish.
Local names for lingcod.
On these boats, a name for vermilion rockfish.

regions.name: Hawaii
regions.intro: Ono, ahi, and aku are everyday fish names in Hawaii. Offshore, a grander is a marlin with four figures on the scale.

terms.meaning: A marlin that weighs at least 1,000 pounds. Hawaii’s list includes blue and black marlin.
The Hawaiian name for wahoo.
A local name for yellowfin tuna and bigeye tuna.
The Hawaiian name for skipjack tuna.
The local name for jacks of at least 10 pounds, including giant, bluefin, and black trevally.
The local name for shortbill spearfish.
A Hawaiian name for greater amberjack.
The local name for jacks under 10 pounds; the larger fish are called ulua.

regions.name: Mexico and Baja California
regions.intro: A Baja captain may call out dorado or pez gallo. Those mean dolphinfish and roosterfish, two very different fights.

terms.meaning: The local name for dolphinfish, also called mahi-mahi.
The Spanish name for roosterfish.
A La Paz name for yellowtail jack.
The local name for leopard grouper.
The local name for mullet snapper.
A Baja name for Gulf grouper.

regions.name: Caribbean, Bahamas, Belize, and Yucatán flats
regions.intro: The classic flats slam follows bonefish, permit, and tarpon across this region. The grey ghost is the bonefish you keep trying to see.

terms.meaning: A bonefish, permit, and tarpon caught in one day; this is the classic Yucatán and Belize flats combination.
A bonefish, permit, tarpon, and snook caught in one day. IGFA lists this combination from Mexico, Belize, and Cuba.
A nickname for bonefish in Belize and the Bahamas, where its camouflage makes it hard to spot.
A young tarpon, smaller than the large migratory fish that visit the bays.

regions.name: Central America’s Pacific coast
regions.intro: A sailfish and one marlin give you two billfish species. A grand slam needs a third species that same day.

terms.meaning: Three different billfish species caught in one day. Off Quepos, a usual combination is sailfish, blue marlin, and black or striped marlin.
One angler catches four eligible billfish species in one calendar day under IGFA rules; sailfish plus blue, black, and striped marlin qualifies.
A Panama name for roosterfish, also called pez gallo.
A Panama name for Pacific crevalle jack.
The Spanish name for dolphinfish in Panama’s sport-fish list.

regions.name: South America: Amazon, Argentina, and offshore waters
regions.intro: The Amazon has peacock names of its own. Farther south, the golden dorado earns the name tiger of the rivers.

terms.meaning: The Brazilian name for the large speckled peacock bass, Cichla temensis.
Two local names for Cichla temensis peacock bass.
The local name for Cichla orinocensis, the butterfly or Orinoco peacock bass.
A local name for Cichla monoculus peacock bass.
The Amazon name for arapaima, a huge freshwater fish that anglers also pursue with flies.
Tiger of the rivers: an Argentine nickname for golden dorado.
The IGFA lifetime set: arawana, dorado, payara, peacock, redtail catfish, sorubim, and trahira, caught by one angler under IGFA rules.

regions.name: UK and Ireland
regions.intro: Salmon anglers use names that tell you a fish’s life stage. In Ireland, a specimen also has a formal award meaning.

terms.meaning: An Atlantic salmon that returns to freshwater after one winter at sea.
An older Atlantic salmon that returns after multiple sea winters, usually in spring or early summer.
An Atlantic salmon after it has spawned, usually thin and in poor condition.
For an Irish Specimen Fish Committee claim, a fish that meets its species’ published weight or length threshold and evidence rules.
The hooked jaw that male salmon develop as they approach the time to spawn.
The Welsh name for sea trout, the sea-run form of brown trout.

regions.name: Scandinavia: Norway and Denmark
regions.intro: Norwegian salmon talk sorts fish by size. Danish sea-trout names tell you whether a fish has spawned or stayed at sea.

terms.meaning: A small Atlantic salmon under 3 kilograms in Norwegian catch records.
A medium Atlantic salmon from 3 to 7 kilograms in Norwegian catch records.
A large Atlantic salmon over 7 kilograms in Norwegian catch records.
Norwegian local names for small Atlantic salmon, usually back after one year at sea.
A small, silver Danish sea trout that has not yet reached sexual maturity.
A Danish sea trout that skips a season of spawning and stays in the sea.
A sea trout back at sea after it has spawned, often thin while it recovers.

regions.name: Australia
regions.intro: A metre barra is a clear size milestone. Names such as croc, hoodie, and elbow slapper are the sort you hear after a good catch.

terms.meaning: A barramundi at least one metre long; the catch earns a place in a metre barra club.
A common angler’s name for mulloway.
A large flathead; croc usually means an especially big one.
A large yellowtail kingfish, often over a metre long. The nickname has no fixed cutoff.
A small yellowtail kingfish.
A big whiting, imagined with its tail at your elbow when you hold its head.
A juvenile mulloway.
Names for a small snapper.
A trip with zero fish caught.

regions.name: New Zealand
regions.intro: A pannie and a moocher are both snapper. Kiwi anglers also shorten kingfish, skipjack, marlin, and swordfish into familiar dockside names.

terms.meaning: A pan-sized snapper.
A big snapper, especially the trophy fish anglers seek around rocky ground.
Short for yellowtail kingfish.
Short for skipjack tuna.
In this New Zealand usage, a striped marlin.
Short for swordfish.

regions.name: Southern Africa
regions.intro: A leerie is a garrick, and a shad is the fish anglers elsewhere call bluefish. The local names change along the coast.

terms.meaning: Names for kob, especially dusky kob, also known overseas as mulloway.
Names for leerfish, also called leervis.
South African names for bluefish.
Names for white musselcracker.
Names for black musselcracker.
Names for white steenbras.
A local nickname for cobia.
Rock-and-surf anglers’ shorthand for bony fish, in contrast to their non-eds category of sharks and rays.

regions.name: Kenya and East African billfish waters
regions.intro: Kenyan crews can put several billfish species together in one day. A boat slam can include catches from different anglers.

terms.meaning: Three billfish species in one day. A Watamu boat combination is sailfish, blue marlin, and striped marlin.
Four billfish species in one day. A Watamu boat combination adds swordfish to sailfish, blue marlin, and striped marlin.
Five billfish species in one day; a Kenyan boat combination is sailfish, blue, black, and striped marlin, plus swordfish.

regions.name: Seychelles flats
regions.intro: A GT, a bonefish, and a trigger can make an Alphonse slam. The local reports also celebrate four-fish super slams.

terms.meaning: One Alphonse version pairs a bonefish, giant trevally, and yellowmargin triggerfish, caught by one angler in one day.
An Alphonse combination of permit, yellowmargin triggerfish, bonefish, and giant trevally, caught by one angler in one day.
Short names for giant trevally.
An angler’s name for titan triggerfish.

regions.name: Japan
regions.intro: In Japan, a fish can get a new name as it grows. The names and rough size bands also change between Kantō and Kansai.

terms.meaning: A fish whose name changes as it grows, such as Japanese amberjack or Japanese sea bass.
A small Japanese sea bass, roughly 30 centimetres or less in Honda’s Kantō and Kansai examples.
A medium Japanese sea bass, roughly 30–60 centimetres: fukko in Kantō, hane in Kansai.
The adult-size name for Japanese sea bass, roughly 60 centimetres and up in these examples.
Names for young Japanese amberjack around 40 centimetres: inada in Kantō, hamachi in Kansai.
Names for larger Japanese amberjack around 60 centimetres: warasa in Kantō, mejiro in Kansai.
The adult-size name for Japanese amberjack, around 80 centimetres and up in these examples.
An angler’s name for a large black sea bream over 50 centimetres.

regions.name: Southeast Asia: Malaysia
regions.intro: Toman and sebarau are familiar targets on Malaysian freshwater trips. Kelah is the local mahseer name that many river anglers hope to add.

terms.meaning: The Malay name for giant snakehead.
The local name for hampala barb, also called jungle perch.
A Malaysian name for mahseer.
The Malay name for striped snakehead.
